extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians in arithmetic geometry and number theory familiar with Mochizuki's IUT framework
extracted.subtask_description: Extracting and applying the section-13 standards for constructing and normalising log-volumes, forming Kummer isomorphisms, and ensuring compatibility across log-links, Frobenioids, and multiradial representations in Mochizuki-style IUT. Focus is on the definitions/normalisations, compatibility requirements, and the handling of indeterminacies used in proofs (eg. Corollary 13.13).

rubrics_metrics.name: Packet-normalisation of log-volumes
rubrics_metrics.description: We shall refer to this normalisation as the packet-normalisation: these log-volumes are normalised in such a manner that multiplication by p_v corresponds to (cid:0) log(p_v) (resp. + log(p_v)) on the log-volume (cf. Remark 13.3.1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply packet-normalisation to the pv-adic (and radial/Archimedean) log-volumes on each direct summand so that multiplication by p_v has the specified effect on the log-volume. Under this normalisation, the log-volume of the given local holomorphic integral structures (as in Proposition 13.3 (2)) is equal to zero. (Reference: Proposition 13.10 (1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Procession-normalisation of log-volumes
rubrics_metrics.description: We shall refer to this normalisation as the procession-normalisation: when working with collections of capsules in a procession, normalise log-volumes on the products of M((cid:0)) associated to the various capsules by taking the average over the various capsules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For procession-level constructions, compute log-volumes on product spaces by averaging the packet-normalised log-volumes across the capsules in the procession. Use this averaged normalisation whenever forming global/progression-level comparisons (appears in Proposition 13.10 (1) and (2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Local Holomorphic Packets determine log-volumes
rubrics_metrics.description: The pvQ-adic log-volume (resp. radial log-volume) on each direct summand of I_Q((cid:11)F_vQ), I_Q(S_j+1; j F_vQ) with the normalised weights determines log-volumes M(I_Q((...))) -> R, and the log-volume of each of the local holomorphic integral structures given by the integral structures of Proposition 13.3 (2) is equal to zero.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct local log-volumes from the local pv-adic and Archimedean data with the specified normalisations; check that the integral structures specified yield zero log-volume. These local constructions form the building blocks for mono-analytic and global log-volumes (Prop.13.10 (1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mono-analytic compatibility of log-volumes
rubrics_metrics.description: By applying the pvQ-adic (resp. radial) log-volume and adjusting discrepancies between local holomorphic integral structures and the mono-analytic integral structures, one obtains log-volumes on mono-analytic log-shells which are compatible with the log-volumes of the local holomorphic theory via the natural poly-isomorphisms of Proposition 13.4 (1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct mono-analytic log-volumes functorially from D'-prime-strips; ensure compatibility with local holomorphic log-volumes under the poly-isomorphisms. When mono-analyticising an F-prime-strip procession, average packet-normalised log-volumes to get procession-normalised mono-analytic log-volumes (Prop.13.10 (2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Global compatibility and invariance of global log-volume
rubrics_metrics.description: The global log-volume (sum of local log-volumes) log_{S_j+1;V_Q} : M(I_Q(S_j+1 F_VQ)) -> R is invariant under multiplication by elements of (yM~_mod)(...) (product formula) and permutations of S, and equals the degree of the arithmetic line bundle determined by the associated object (cf. Proposition 13.10 (3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When forming the global log-volume by adding local contributions, restrict to components with zero log-volume for all but finitely many places. Verify product-formula invariance and that the resulting global value matches the arithmetic degree under the chosen normalisation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Log-link compatibility of log-volumes
rubrics_metrics.description: The log-volumes described in (1)-(3) determine log-volumes on the objects appearing in the construction of the local/global LGP-/lgp-monoids/Frobenioids in F-prime-strips relative to the log-link n;m full_log -> n;m (and these indexed log-volumes are compatible across (n,m) in the sense of Proposition 12.2 (2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure that log-volumes transform according to the formulas referenced (Prop.5.2 (5.1), Prop.5.4 (5.2)) when passing along log-links; this compatibility implies one need not worry about how many times log-links are applied when evaluating log-volumes in the log-Kummer correspondence (Prop.13.10(4)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction of vertically coric global LGP/lgp-Frobenioids and Kummer isomorphisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Functorial algorithms produce vertically coric (etale-like) number fields, monoids, and (pre-)Frobenioids equipped with natural isomorphisms and Kummer isomorphisms relating labels such as M~_mod, M~_MOD, F~_mod, F~_MOD for the D-(cid:2)(cid:1)-Hodge theatre n;◦HT (Prop.13.11 (1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the constructions of Proposition 13.8 to etale-like F-prime-strips and full log-links to produce the vertically coric objects. Check naturality with respect to the D-Hodge theatre and compatibility with the non-vertically coric algorithms (compatibility references: Cor.11.21, Cor.11.23, Prop.13.8).

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-interference with local integers (log-Kummer actions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Actions of multiplicative groups of non-zero elements of number fields on modules are effected not via a single Kummer isomorphism (which fails compatibility with log-links) but via the totality of pre-composites of Kummer isomorphisms with iterates of the p_v-adic logarithmic/Archimedean exponential parts of log-links; the only potential relations between these actions via log-links are indeterminacies by multiplication by roots of unity, which are sent to addition by zero by the p_v-adic logarithm (so no indeterminacy at the next step) (Prop.13.11 (2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement group actions through the full family of pre-composed Kummer maps combined with the appropriate logarithmic/exponential parts. Verify that indeterminacies from roots of unity are eliminated when transferring across log-links (use Remark 10.12.1, Def.12.1 (2),(4), Prop.12.2 (2) for quotient discussions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Frobenioid-theoretic log-Kummer correspondences
rubrics_metrics.description: Kummer isomorphisms induce isomorphisms of (pre-)Frobenioids which are mutually compatible with the log-links of the LGP-Gaussian log-theta-lattice and induce Kummer isomorphisms of associated F-prime-strips compatible as m varies over Z (Prop.13.11 (3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When passing to Frobenioid-level statements, ensure the induced isomorphisms respect the log-links and the translational symmetry m -> m+1; check compatibility of MOD/LGP-labelled objects (multiplicative portion) and note upper semi-compatibility issues with mod/lgp-labelled objects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification and treatment of indeterminacies (Indet xy, Indet !, Indet ")
rubrics_metrics.description: Three kinds of indeterminacies are singled out: (Indet xy) permutative indeterminacy in etale-transport (automorphisms of processions), (Indet !) horizontal indeterminacy in Kummer detachment (actions by Isomet etc), and (Indet ") vertical indeterminacy in Kummer detachment (log-related descent data from Z to F1) (Remarks 13.13.1 and surrounding text).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When comparing objects/isomorphisms one must admit these indeterminacies: (Indet xy) allows permutation/aut of proc; (Indet !) describes integral-structure/horizontal ambiguity; (Indet ") encodes vertical logarithmic ambiguity. Many compatibility claims and volume comparisons are made only up to admitting these indeterminacies (e.g., Theorem 13.12, Cor.13.13).

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation invariance of log-Kummer correspondence (m -> m+1)
rubrics_metrics.description: The global log-Kummer correspondence between multiplicative groups and their actions on labelled I_Q((cid:0)) objects is invariant with respect to the translation symmetries m -> m+1 of the n-th column of the LGP-Gaussian log-theta-lattice (Prop.13.11 (2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exploit the translation symmetry when constructing or comparing Kummer correspondences; use it to propagate compatibilities across columns and to argue that certain indeterminacies vanish under the p_v-adic logarithm at the next step.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compatibility of Kummer isomorphisms with log-volumes and log-links
rubrics_metrics.description: The Kummer-induced isomorphisms of local mono-analytic tensor packets, splitting monoids, and global number-field/Frobenioid data are compatible with the respective log-volumes by Proposition 13.10 (2), and this compatibility persists (up to the admitted indeterminacies) with the log-links of the n-th column (Theorem 13.12 (2),(3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When transporting objects via Kummer isomorphisms, check that log-volumes are preserved/compatible (use Prop.13.10(2) and Theorem 13.12 statements). Note that mod/lgp-labelled objects (involving both multiplicative and additive structure) only enjoy upper semi-compatibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiradial representation components and allowed indeterminacies
rubrics_metrics.description: The multiradial representation (Theorem 13.12) consists of: (Shells) unit portion/mono-analytic containers equipped with procession-normalised log-volumes; (ThVals) theta-values splitting monoids acting multiplicatively; (NFs) global number-field portions with Frobenioids. The constructed data n;◦RLGP is regarded up to (Indet xy) and (Indet !), and permutation symmetries induce compatible poly-isomorphisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assemble multiradial data from local shells, theta-values, and global number-field pieces. Record and track the two types of indeterminacies (etale-transport and horizontal Kummer detachment) when asserting equality or isomorphism of multiradial objects; verify functoriality under Proc and permutation symmetries (Theorem 13.12 (1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Log-volume estimates for (cid:2)-pilot and q-pilot objects (Corollary 13.13)
rubrics_metrics.description: Define procession-normalised mono-analytic log-volumes (0_j log((cid:2))_j) for (cid:2)-pilot objects and (0_j log(q)_j) for q-pilot objects (the latter >0). Then one obtains (0_j log(q)_j) >= (cid:20) (0_j log((cid:2))_j) (and related explicit inequalities; note also 0_j log((cid:2))_j < 1) (Cor.13.13).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare log-volumes of q-pilot and (cid:2)-pilot objects after admitting the indeterminacies (Indet xy), (Indet !), (Indet "). Use Kummer isomorphisms and LGP-link compatibilities to transport labelled objects to place their log-volumes in direct comparison; this comparison underlies the proof of Theorem 0.1 (via Prop.1.2, Prop.1.15 and Cor.13.13).

rubrics_metrics.name: Upper semi-compatibility vs precise compatibility distinctions
rubrics_metrics.description: Objects labelled MOD/LGP (multiplicative-only) enjoy precise log-Kummer correspondence and are well-suited to log-volume computation; mod/lgp-labelled objects (both multiplicative and additive) only enjoy upper semi-compatibility and are ill-suited to log-volume computations (Remark following Prop.13.11 and later tables).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer working with MOD/LGP-labelled (multiplicative) objects when exact log-volume computations and compatibility claims are required. Treat mod/lgp-labelled objects with caution: expect only upper semi-compatibility and mild indeterminacies affecting volume calculations.
